title.narrative: Greater Mekong Subregion Border Areas Health Project

description.narrative: The project will improve access to quality health services for populations residing in and migrating across Banteay Meanchey province in Cambodia's northwest. Banteay Meanchey province serves as a transit point for migrants departing to and returning from Thailand. It also serves as a destination point for internal migrants seeking opportunities in the province's special economic zones (SEZs) and informal sector industries. Populations residing in and migrating through Banteay Meanchey are susceptible to mobility-linked health threats, including communicable diseases and environmental and social risk factors. The project will invest in new health facilities and equipment, expand the availability of clinical care and migrant-specific health services, improve the quality of the health workforce, and extend health-care-related financial protection to migrants.

National Quality Enhancement Monitoring index scores reach at least 75% for Mongkol Borei Provincial Hospital and at least 60% for Poipet Referral Hospital Progress/Status: Semester 1 2024: In semester 1-2024, the national quality enhancement monitoring index score for Mongkol Borei provincial hospital is 60.38% and Poipet referral hospital 45.29%. Semester 2 2024: In semester 2-2024, Mongkol Borei provincial hospital is 64.11% and Poipet referral hospital is 32.74%. In Poi Pet hospital 7 of 11 main standard groups decreased the score comparing to previous assessment. Semester 1 2025: Mongkol Borei provincial hospital scored 78.43% and Poipet referral hospital scored 52.64%. In semester 2 2025: Mokol Borei provincial hospital scored 86.22% and Poi Pet referral hospital scored 79.04%. In semester 1 2026: Mokol Borei provincial hospital scored 84.48% and Poi Pet referral hospital scored 73.01%. Data Source: National Quality Enhancement Monitoring Tool-2 Actual value:

Outpatient service utilization at Poipet Referral Hospital by female and male migrants increased by 10% Progress/Status: Based on the data from PMRS reporting the number of patients from outside the catchment areas. In 2024, the number of migrant access outpatient service is 1,299 (Female:802). In 2025, the number of migrant access outpatient service is 2,578 (Female: 1,512). Data Source: Information system of Poipet Referral Hospital Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Health financial protection for migrant populations improved Indicator: By 2026, gender-responsive adjustment to the SHI program to improve access by vulnerable female and male migrants approved by the NSPC for small-scale implementation in one demonstration province Progress/Status: The project signed a contract with the consulting firm (SBK) to conduct Analytical Work on Social Health Insurance (CS04) on 27 June 2025. The consulting firm submitted the fieldwork completion report on 18 February 2026. The draft assessment report is expected to be submitted to the project in April 2026. The assessments and recommendations for adjustments to the regulations, systems, or processes of the SHI program are scheduled to be completed in Q2 2026. Data Source: NSPC-issued decisions Actual value:

Output: Health service delivery in selected border areas strengthened Indicator: By 2028, At least 75% of doctors and nurses staffing outpatient departments at Mongkol Borei Provincial Hospital and Poipet Referral Hospital report improved skills for identifying and providing referral options to people affected by gender-based violence Progress/Status: The project engaged a training specialist in Q4 2024. The training needs assessment was conducted in Q4 2024, and the report was finalized in Q1 2025. The advertisement for the workforce training consulting firm was published on 12 July 2025, with a closing date of 28 August 2025 (Q3 2025). The shortlisted EOI evaluation was approved by the Procurement Review Committee (PRC) on 16 January 2026 and submitted to ADB on 21 January 2026. ADB issued a no-objection for the shortlisted EOIs on 13 March 2026. The training activities are expected to be rolled out in Q2 2026. Data Source: Project training assessments and evaluation reports Actual value:

Output: Health service delivery in selected border areas strengthened Indicator: By 2028, One new migrant health center, including services for sexual and reproductive health and rights, gender-based violence, and maternal and child health, operational at each of Mongkol Borei Provincial Hospital and Poipet Referral Hospital Progress/Status: The contract for the Detailed Design and Construction Supervision (DDCS) firm was signed on 12 March 2025. The design incorporates health medical records and services for sexual and reproductive health and rights, gender-based violence, and maternal and child health for all people, including migrants. The detailed engineering design and bidding documents were approved by ADB on 20 March 2026. The civil works contractor packages are expected to be advertised on 6 April 2026 (Q2 2026), with construction works scheduled for completion in Q2 2028 and facilities becoming operational by Q1 2029. Data Source: Annual project monitoring reports Actual value:

Output: Health service delivery in selected border areas strengthened Indicator: By 2028, One new outpatient-inpatient building at each of Mongkol Borei Provincial Hospital and Poipet Referral Hospital that incorporates gender-responsive and climate-smart design features operational Progress/Status: The contract for the Detailed Design and Construction Supervision firm was signed on 12 March 2025. The consulting firm finalized and submitted the detailed engineering design (DED) report and bidding documents on 12 December 2025. The detailed engineering design and bidding documents were approved by ADB on 20 March 2026. The civil works contractor packages are expected to be advertised on 6 April 2026, with construction works scheduled for completion in Q2 2028 Data Source: Acceptance minutes for each facility Actual value:

Output: Systems for integrated and gender-responsive delivery of health services within and across borders enhanced Indicator: By 2025, provincial health departments implement at least two cross-border activities annually on infectious disease control and health service access for cross-border migrants Achievement: 4 Progress/Status: Activities commenced in 2024 with the project organizing a cross-border meeting between Cambodia (Banteay Meanchey and Battambang Provinces) and Thailand (Sa Kaeo Province) in Q4 2024. Under AWPB 2025, the PHD plan to organize 2 cross border activities. Due to border tension between Cambodia-Thailand these activities will not be implemented in 2025. In Q4 2025, The project has conducted an assessment on the possibility of shifting the cross-border meetings from Thailand to the Lao PDR. Data Source: Annual project reports

Output: Systems for integrated and gender-responsive delivery of health services within and across borders enhanced Indicator: By 2028, a pilot to provide female migrants from Cambodia with portable access to their ePHR, including information supporting continuity of perinatal care, when in Thailand and Cambodia implemented and evaluated Progress/Status: A situational analysis was conducted to provide recommendations for revisions to the scope and implementation schedule for the Electronic Personal Health Record (ePHR) activity. The TOR for recruiting consulting services for design and implementation of Unique Health Identifier and ePHR was submitted to ADB for review on 23 May 2025, and approval was received on 9 July 2025. The advertisement for recruiting the consulting firm was published on 9 August 2025 with a closing date of 9 September 2025. The shortlisted EOI evaluation was approved by the Procurement Review Committee (PRC) on 16 January 2026 and submitted to ADB on 21 January 2026. ADB issued a no-objection for the shortlisted EOIs on 17 February 2026. The consulting firm is likely to be awarded in Q2 2026.
Data Source: Endline project survey Actual value:

Output: Health financial protection for migrant populations improved Indicator: By 2024, pre-departure enrollment in a low-cost migrant health insurance scheme that provides coverage in Thailand and Cambodia available to Cambodia's female migrants Progress/Status: The Migrant Health fund (M-Fund) has commenced operations in Poipet, including the setup of a working space at Poipet Hospital. To date, approximately 1,178, including 672 females, individuals from Banteay Meanchey have enrolled in the M-Fund, with some members receiving health care services at Poipet Hospital. The project will continue to raise migrant's awareness of and access to M-Fund ‘s services. Data Source: Annual project monitoring reports Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y

Output: Health financial protection for migrant populations improved Indicator: By 2028, revised SHI program that is more gender responsive and facilitates enrollment of eligible female and male migrants implemented Progress/Status: The project has signed the contract with consulting firm (SBK) to conduct Analytical Work: Social Health Insurance (CS 04) on 27 June 2025. The consulting firm submitted the fieldwork completion report on 18 February 2026. The assessments and recommendations for adjustments to the regulations, systems, or processes of the SHI program are scheduled to be completed in Q2 2026. The implementation is scheduled in Q4 2026.
